findings.location: Lemma 6.6 pp31-33, particularly p32 first paragraph; (6.1)-(6.2) p25, (6.12)-(6.13) p29; application Lemma 6.7 p33
findings.claim: v-c0 psi satisfies the homogeneous equation required by Proposition 6.2(iii).
findings.evidence: Smooth symmetric far-field perturbation Ktilde=k0[1+eps(a(x)b(y)+a(y)b(x))], separated supports, g=1 on supp b, yields L0 psi=2 eps a(x)(1-psi(x)) integral b(y)k0(x-y)dy>0. For the positive L0-harmonic comparison v, c0=average(v/psi)>0, so L0(v-c0 psi) is nonzero.
findings.scope: Confirmed false proof inference in the core Campanato chain to Theorems 6.8,6.1,1.6 and Green applications. No counterexample to the claimed final regularity or to the complete Lemma 6.6 inequality established.
findings.repair: Supply an inhomogeneous relative-barrier estimate controlling the retained forcing, or harmonize operators and reprove the closeness step. Full repair not certified.

findings.claim: The printed X space can replace the weighted Lq source hypothesis in the main theorems.
findings.evidence: The positive support exponent makes all H^{-s} data on the bounded testing region admissible. n=2,s=p=1/2,q=infinity, Omega=B2, u=eta|x|^{-1/4}, eta=1 on B2 and compactly supported B3, f=(-Delta)^s u in B1. u is in H^s and weighted L1, f is a positive locally integrable dual datum and has finite printed X norm, but u is unbounded.
findings.scope: False asserted extension of the main regularity conclusion; not a counterexample to the original weighted-Lq theorem.
findings.repair: Use the negative support exponent to encode (3.1); alternatively formulate and prove the exact local dual scale bounds needed. The original positive-exponent extension must be withdrawn.

findings.location: Theorem 1.1 lower-bound proof, Case 2 pp52-53; Case 3 reuses it
findings.claim: A Harnack chain gives a positive lower bound for the auxiliary u at x outside Omega_{R/8}.
findings.evidence: Omega=B10((0,10)), x=(0,3/4), y=(0,7/4), R=2, z=(0,4), kappa=1/8. All Case 2 geometric inequalities hold. x lies outside the harmonic domain Omega_{R/4}=Omega cap B_{1/2}(0) and outside the nonzero data ball, so the displayed exterior data force u(x)=0.
findings.scope: The positive intermediate lower bound is false in an admissible case, leaving the stated proof of a principal Green-function bound incomplete. The Green-function conclusion is not disproved.
findings.repair: Propagate a lower bound for G itself on a chain staying away from the pole, or change the auxiliary domain/radii and justify all geometric regimes. Full global repair not supplied.

findings.claim: The first oscillation after subtracting the source-defined average has decay exponent min(2s-n/q,1+sigma-epsilon), possibly greater than one.
findings.evidence: n=2,s=3/4,sigma=1/4,epsilon=1/8,q=infinity,u=x1,constant fractional kernel,f=0. Local energy and tail hypotheses hold. For every constant m, reflection symmetry gives average_Brho |x1-m| >= average_Brho |x1| = 4rho/(3pi). This lower bound holds when m is the source-defined average of |u|, so the left side of Lemma 5.5 is not O(rho^{9/8}).
findings.scope: False auxiliary estimate. The later uses for Theorem 1.7 and barrier closeness target exponents below s<1, so no additional principal conclusion is disproved.
findings.repair: For noninteger exponents above one, cap the first-oscillation exponent at one; higher Campanato exponents require affine approximants. The critical integer endpoint also requires the restriction in P5.
findings.historical_calculation_scope: The retained initial script evaluates the absolute first moment of x1, equivalently oscillation about signed mean zero, not the exact oscillation about average |x1|. Its ratio and limit calculations apply to the lower bound proved here. No new computation is claimed.

findings.claim: The estimate includes C^1 at the critical source exponent.
findings.evidence: n=2,s=3/4,q=4,sigma=1/4,epsilon=1/8. f=(1+cos theta)r^{-1/2}[log(e/r)]^{-1/2} on r<1/4 is nonnegative L4. Its Riesz potential u=I_{3/2}f has finite local energy and tail but u(te1)-u(0) divided by t tends to infinity: the odd angular component gives integral dr/(r sqrt(log(e/r))), while the radial component contributes O(1) to this quotient.
findings.scope: Critical interior auxiliary statement false. The main boundary targets are below one; Corollary 1.2 uses homogeneous equations and s>1/2, so this example does not refute those conclusions.
findings.repair: Exclude the integer endpoint or use a justified endpoint space/weaker Holder exponent.

findings.location: Example immediately after Theorem 1.8 p9; frozen kernel (1.9) p7
findings.claim: The displayed variable a_x symmetric kernel class satisfies the frozen homogeneity assumption.
findings.evidence: a_x(theta)=2+eps cos x1, 0<eps<1. The kernel is symmetric, elliptic and smooth under simultaneous translations, but K0(h)|h|^{n+2s}=4+eps(1+cos h1) is not homogeneous of degree zero.
findings.scope: Invalid illustrative class; not a counterexample to Theorem 1.8 under its explicit extra hypothesis.
findings.repair: Impose actual frozen homogeneity, e.g. an x-independent even angular density, or weaken the claimed example.

findings.claim: A supersolution is obtained from (2.2) by replacing u alone by -u.
findings.evidence: With f=1 and u=0, both printed inequalities hold, although Lu=0 differs from f. Correct reversal requires (u,f) -> (-u,-f).
findings.scope: Literal weak-solution definition is inconsistent with the equation. Counterexamples P2/P5 use nonnegative f and exact equality, so they also satisfy both printed inequalities.
findings.repair: Reverse the sign of f as well, or state E(u,varphi)>=<f,varphi> explicitly.

findings.location: Poisson representation (9.6) p53; normalization (1.1) p1 and Definition 9.1 p50
findings.claim: P(x,z)=integral_Omega G(x,y)K(z,y)dy with the given L=2 p.v. normalization.
findings.evidence: For smooth exterior data g supported away from Omega, the zero exterior extension of u solves Lv=2 integral g(z)K(x,z)dz. Inverting L gives P=2 integral GK. For g=1 on Omega^c, the printed kernel has total mass 1/2 instead of 1.
findings.scope: Exact representation normalization is wrong; multiplicative constants in the two-sided Poisson estimates can absorb the factor.
findings.repair: Insert factor 2 in (9.6), consistently with (1.1) and the inverse Green definition.

acceptance_revision.notes: Corrected existing P4 from an unjustified equality to a rigorous reflection-symmetry lower bound under the actual absolute-value-average notation. Primary actually viewed source pp.10 and 23. P4 remains confirmed Minor; all other reported classifications are retained after focused checks. Initial calculation script, output and execution receipt are preserved unchanged and explicitly limited to their actual mathematical scope.

focused_checks.reason: Primary checked short-jump agreement and tilde-L psi=0 on p.25, L-harmonicity required by Proposition 6.2(iii), local freezing (6.12) on p.29, and the explicit invocation on p.32 with dependencies pp.33,36. For separated smooth supports and exterior g=1 on supp b, the operator difference gives L0 psi=2 delta a(1-psi) integral b k0 >0. Positive v yields the actual c0=average(v/psi)>0, including the source's absolute-value convention. The freezing point can have a=b=0 while the small ball meets positive a. Thus the omitted forcing occurs within the stated setup. The report claims failure of the homogeneous proof inference, not falsity of the complete Campanato inequality or boundary theorem.

Primary read Remark 3.2 and the X norm on pp.14-15 and the localized Theorem 1.6 on p.5. The positive support factor admits every energy-dual functional on the bounded testing region. The cutoff power |x|^{-1/4} at n=2,s=1/2 has positive dyadic energy exponent 1/2, finite tail, and positive locally integrable fractional source; the Riesz-power gamma factors are all positive. Omega=B2 is allowed because Theorem 1.6 does not require the origin on its boundary. The example refutes the asserted X-extension, not the original weighted-Lq source theorem. The sign change is necessary but not certified as a complete new theorem.

Primary checked every Case 2 condition on pp.52-53 for the stated disk and points: d(x)=3/4<1<=7/4=d(y), R=2, |y-z|=9/4, |x0-z|=4, and the radius-1/4 data ball is outside B2 and inside Omega. The point x is outside both the harmonic domain B_{1/2}(0) cap Omega and the nonzero data ball, so u(x)=0 exactly. The claimed positive auxiliary value is false. This is a core lower-bound proof gap; no false final Green bound or complete repair is claimed.

Primary actually viewed source pp.10 and 23. The original equality used signed mean zero, whereas the source defines the average of |u|. Reflection pairs x1 and -x1 prove average |x1-m| >= average |x1|=4rho/(3pi) for every constant m. This universal lower bound, now in the report/findings, still contradicts rho^{9/8} for the admissible affine harmonic function with finite tail at s=3/4. The retained script/output evaluate the first absolute moment and its ratio to the claimed scale; they do not compute the exact oscillation about average |u| and have not been rerun or relabelled. The repair wording preserves the separate integer-endpoint issue.

Primary checked the literal integer endpoint in Proposition 3.5 and the Riesz example. The radial L4 integral is finite; Fourier energy is integrable at zero and infinity, giving the local energy class without falsely asserting global L2. Pairing the odd angular component makes its positive difference quotient diverge by Fatou, while radial symmetry bounds the other quotient using the inner/outer split. The example therefore fails Lipschitz and ordinary C1 regularity at the printed exponent. Main boundary exponents are below one and the stated homogeneous gradient application avoids this example.

Primary substituted a_x(theta)=2+delta cos(x1) into the exact symmetric freeze on p.7 and read the extra homogeneity requirement/example on p.9. The coefficient 4+delta(1+cos h1) varies radially although symmetry, ellipticity and simultaneous-translation Holder bounds hold. This excludes the advertised general example, not Theorem 1.8 with its actual extra assumption.

Primary checked Definition 2.1 on p.11: replacing only u by -u accepts u=0,f=1 as both sub- and supersolution. Reversing f as well restores the intended inequality. P2/P5 use nonnegative f and exact equality, so their validity does not exploit the definition typo.

Primary compared L=2 p.v. on p.1, the inverse-Green definition on p.50, and (9.6) on p.53. Zero extension of an L-harmonic function with smooth distant exterior data has forcing 2 integral gK, hence inversion yields P=2 integral GK. The missing factor affects the exact representation; estimates up to unspecified multiplicative constants are not refuted.
